description: n512 B640 dominant shape spends ~16% on NON-math support kernels no worker touches: classify_convert_n512 (5.4%, one 167us launch that FP32->FP16 converts + classifies good/bad), build_Minv_blk4 (8%, the T-factor inverse), fill_R_zero_tail_n512 (2.8%, 85us zeroing R's sub-diagonal). These are format/bookkeeping, gate-safe (no accuracy risk). Fuse and shrink them: merge classify+convert into the panel's first load (convert on the fly), fold fill_R_zero_tail into the apply epilogue (write zeros while writing R), and cut build_Minv cost (cheaper batched TRSM or fold into the trailing GEMM). Eliminate separate launches/passes over the B*n*n data. Hits 5/12 of geomean off the clean remote-valid baseline.

Y-fold (Y=M@W on-chip) in build_Minv_blk4 for n512 good path, maxrest=512 (all outer applies). Numerically identical (validate residuals byte-for-byte == parent). REGRESSION: build_Minv_blk4 244->1283us (8->31.7% on shape3) -- single-CTA on-chip Y at wide rest (up to 448, K=64) serializes far worse than cuBLAS batched mmb_Y. shape3 3161->4126us; geomean 1638->1730.

Narrow Y-fold (maxrest=64): fold Y=M@W on-chip in build_Minv_blk4 ONLY for the last outer apply (rest<=64). shape3 3161->3176us (+0.5%), geomean 1638->1644 (+0.35%) -- NEUTRAL/slightly worse; single-CTA 64x64 Y ~= the cuBLAS mmb_Y it replaces on this occupancy-rich B=640 shape. Y-fold does not pay; build_Minv stays on cuBLAS Y.

Branchless-per-chunk rank-reveal in classify_convert_n512: 1 chunk max-abs test vs 8 per-elem compares (col0 mult-of-8 => all 8 elems in one 64-wide block-col). BIT-IDENTICAL, validate==parent. classify_convert 166.8->162.6us; shape3 3161->3148us (-0.43%); geomean 1637.9->1634.7 (-0.19%). rr branchiness was minor; convert+col/row sampling still dominate the 162us.

n512 good build_Minv blk4->rblk_gen nlev=2. ncu KEY FINDING: build_Minv_blk4 is LATENCY-bound not occupancy-hidden -- 0.72 waves/SM, 46% occ, 2.7% DRAM, 53% compute. Tried shorter-chain rblk nlev2 (~5 syncs vs blk4 ~12). Numerically identical. shape3 3148->3180us (+1.0%), geomean 1634.7->1637.9 (+0.2%) -- slightly worse; extra parallel merge matmuls offset sync savings. blk4 stays best so far.

n512 good build_Minv rblk_gen nlev=3 (deeper recursion, depth-b/8). Numerically identical (validate PASS). shape3 3148->3242us (+3%), geomean 1634.7->1645.8 -- WORSE than blk4 and nlev=2. nlev sweep {2,3} both regress (extra parallel merge matmuls > chain savings). blk4 4-block-merge remains best for this latency-bound 0.72-wave kernel; chain-restructuring is a dead lever here.

n512 good build_Minv threads/CTA 256->512 (the kernel is <1 wave so per-CTA latency dominates). Numerically identical. shape3 3148->3208us (+1.9%), geomean 1634.7->1640.6 -- WORSE. Serial forward-sub chain doesn't parallelize with more threads; 512 adds idle threads + cuts occupancy. build_Minv thread-count dead (256 best). Combined with the nlev sweep, build_Minv chain/thread restructuring all regress -- the blk4 256-thread config is already its local optimum.

fill_R off-diagonal direct half2 load (drop cp.async 16B smem staging). BIT-IDENTICAL. fill_R 85->122us (+44% SLOWER): direct path does 4-byte half2 global loads vs cp.async's 16-byte chunks -> much worse coalescing. The smem staging IS the optimization. shape3 +1.7%, geomean 1634.7->1644.6 worse. Reverted. fill_R is already near-optimal for a BF16->FP32 convert (72% DRAM).

Drop f[8] array in classify_convert (reference a.x..b.w directly) to cut registers and raise occupancy on the DRAM-bound (82%) kernel. Byte-identical. NEUTRAL: shape3 ~3162us, geomean ~1634.8 (vs trial3 1633.9; first run 1673 was a transient under concurrent-worker host contention, re-run 1634.8). Kernel is bandwidth-bound by fixed ~1GB convert traffic, so register cuts don't raise effective BW. NOTE: host has ~2% run-to-run variance under load -- sub-1% deltas need a confirming re-run.

g_inner_wmma_wmax 32->64: route the last OB-wide w=64,rest=64 apply to on-chip WMMA (recomputes S+M => no build_Minv/mmb_S/mmb_Y for that block). Byte-identical residuals. BIG REGRESSION: shape3 +4.6%, shape9 +13%, shape10 +23%, geomean 1634->1690. Confirms parent's claim -- single-CTA w=64 WMMA full-apply loses badly to cuBLAS batched GEMM (esp rankdef/clustered capped loops). build_Minv+cuBLAS is correct for OB-wide; build_Minv cannot be eliminated via WMMA. Reverted.

__launch_bounds__(256,8) on classify_convert: force 8 blocks/SM (regs<=32) to lift the register-capped 71% occupancy on the DRAM-bound (82%) convert. Byte-identical. NEUTRAL: classify_convert 162.3->161.4us, geomean ~1634.9 (vs trial3 1633.9). The 82%->peak DRAM gap is memory-latency not occupancy; raising occupancy past 71% doesn't help. classify_convert is at its 1GB-traffic floor (671MB FP32 read + 336MB BF16 write, both mandatory).

BEST = trial3 (e9a69f2f9): branchless-per-chunk rank-reveal in classify_convert_n512_kernel. geomean 1637.88->1633.87us (-0.24%, stable across 3 runs 1634.70/1633.93/1633.87), shape3 3161->3158us. BYTE-IDENTICAL residuals (n512 dense factor 0.00854/orth 0.403 vs gate 1.0 -- the comfortable good-path margin the brief asked to hold; every test+invariance shape PASS). Kept HEAD.

KEY FINDING (ncu on shape3): the brief's premise that the 3 support kernels are launch/redundancy-bound does NOT hold -- they are at RESOURCE FLOORS bound by NECESSARY data movement:
- build_Minv_blk4 (7.9%, 244us, 7 launches): LATENCY-bound, 0.72 waves/SM, 46% occ, 2.7% DRAM, 53% compute. The serial forward-sub chain is exposed (GPU is <1 wave: 640 matrices, ~4.3 CTAs/SM, can't add CTAs). NOT occupancy-hidden as the stale code comment claimed.
- classify_convert (5.3%, 162us): DRAM-bound at 82% (6.2TB/s). It is the WHOLE-batch FP32->BF16 convert moving ~1GB (671MB FP32 read + 336MB BF16 write, both mandatory); classify piggybacks free on the convert reads. Fused IS bandwidth-optimal -- a split re-reads.
- fill_R_zero_tail (2.8%, 85us): DRAM-bound at 72% (5.6TB/s), the BF16->FP32 R-upper-triangle convert (~440MB). The cp.async 16B staging IS the optimization.

WHAT REGRESSED (all measured+committed+logged, reverted from HEAD):
- build_Minv Y-fold maxrest=512 (t1): +30% shape3 (on-chip Y serializes at wide rest, build_Minv 244->1283us). maxrest=64 (t2): neutral.
- build_Minv rblk_gen nlev=2 (t4): +0.2%; nlev=3 (t5): +3%. Deeper recursion adds parallel merge matmuls that cost more than the shorter chain saves on this 53%-compute kernel.
- build_Minv threads 256->512 (t6): +1.9% (serial chain doesn't parallelize; more idle threads).
- wmax=64 to route last w=64 OB-wide apply to on-chip WMMA (t9): +4.6%/+13%(s9)/+23%(s10) -- confirms single-CTA w=64 WMMA full-apply loses badly to cuBLAS; build_Minv+cuBLAS cannot be eliminated this way.
- fill_R off-diag direct half2 load (t7): fill_R +44% (direct 4B loads << cp.async 16B; staging is essential).
- classify_convert drop f[8] (t8) + launch_bounds(256,8) (t10): both NEUTRAL (kernel is at its 1GB bandwidth floor; occupancy past 71% doesn't help the 82%->peak gap, which is memory-latency).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not yet reached / would need a different brief):
1. build_Minv is the biggest reducible target BUT bound by the 0.72-wave single-wave latency. The diagonal-inversion phase (minv_diag_invert) uses only b=64 of 256 threads (192 idle); restructuring it to use all threads, or shrinking the ~12 barriers in blk4 without adding merge matmuls, is the only remaining lever -- but that is MATH-kernel surgery (out of this brief's safe-transform scope) and risk-bearing.
2. Reduce CONVERT TRAFFIC (the only thing that helps the bandwidth-bound classify_convert): skip the BF16 convert of the FIRST outer block's panel columns [0,64) and have the panel read FP32 A directly (~5us, 1/8 of the write). Marginal + complex.
3. OB=128 outer block (4 blocks vs 8): fewer/larger build_Minv launches with more per-CTA parallelism -- but it falls off the OB=64-specific fill_R + rank-reveal fast paths and touches the math kernels.
4. Overlap build_Minv with adjacent-block cuBLAS GEMMs via a 2nd CUDA stream -- but the chain is data-dependent within a block AND streams risk the remote leaderboard's queue-API text-scan rejection (per project memory).
HOST NOTE: ~2% run-to-run variance under concurrent workers; sub-1% deltas need a confirming re-run (t8's first run showed a false 1673 transient that re-ran to 1634.8).
